newsitem.title: POLAND: State auditor criticises Polish telecom firm TPSA.
newsitem.headline: State auditor criticises Polish telecom firm TPSA.

text.p: Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) said on Tuesday its probe into the state-owned telecom firm Telekumunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) showed the company was abusing its virtually monopolist position.
The NIK report showed that TPSA has been limiting access of private companies to local telephone markets and was keeping long-distance connection prices at inflated levels.
"A lack of competition was used by the company to increase its highly dominant position on the telecommunications market," the report said.
It said the excessively high prices of long-distance links, which under the current regulations are operated only by TPSA, could have been used to subsidise the local connections.
Long-distance connections are 18 times more expensive than the local ones.
"An opportunity was created for an internal funding of local connections by revenues from long-distance and international connections. Local operators were unable to do this," the report said.
TPSA spokesman Krzysztof Bartnicki was quoted by the public television as saying that TPSA could not reduce long-distance prices because it was undergoing an intensive modernisation programme.
But the NIK report criticised TPSA for passing on the whole burden of its investment plans to its clients regardless of the actual costs of the connections and their maintenance.
The NIK report also alleged that TPSA was in many cases delaying cooperation agreements with local operators.
Under a government plan, TPSA will remain the monopolist on the long-distance connections market until after its privatisation, due to start next year.
According to an agreement with the World Trade Organisation, Poland has to liberalise international connections by the end of 2002.
